# 0.24.0 — 9 November 2026

Minor release on 0.23.0. A Splunk block's `advanced` table validates and deploys again, so catalogues whose rules set a custom alert action's parameters, such as MISP's, pass `validate`. The editor and `opentide tui` check CrowdStrike queries as CQL. The engine is [language-server 0.12.1](https://github.com/opentidehq/language-server/releases/tag/v0.12.1).

## Upgrade

```bash
pip install opentide==0.24.0
export OPENTIDE_REPO_ROOT=/path/to/detection-repo
opentide validate --strict
```

| Before | Now |
|--------|-----|
| 0.21.0 to 0.23.0 refused a Splunk block's `advanced` table (`Extra inputs are not permitted`), so `validate` failed every catalogue holding a rule that set raw `savedsearches.conf` keys, and such a rule could not be deployed | `advanced` validates, and `deploy` sends each key as written, over a value the block sets and under the tenant's modifiers. A `null` value is sent empty (0.20.1 sent the text `None`), a boolean as `1` or `0`; a list or table is refused |
| The editor reported each CrowdStrike query with one `crowdstrike_unsupported` warning | the editor and `opentide tui` report the `cql_*` diagnostics. `validate`, `lint` and MCP `validate_query` still do not check CrowdStrike queries |

It is a minor because it changes what validation accepts (the `advanced` table) and adds a feature (CQL in the editor and the TUI, from language-server 0.12).

## Added

- **The editor and `opentide tui` check CrowdStrike queries as CQL**, the query language of Falcon LogScale and Next-Gen SIEM. `configurations.crowdstrike.query` and hunts with `system: crowdstrike` get the `cql_*` diagnostics, and `opentide lsp start` adds hover, completion and highlighting. `validate`, `lint` and MCP `validate_query` still do not check CrowdStrike queries.

## Changed

- **The engine is [language-server 0.12.1](https://github.com/opentidehq/language-server/releases/tag/v0.12.1), from crates.io.** It adds the CQL language, its Tide catalog accepts a Splunk block's `advanced` table, so `opentide-lsp` run on its own agrees with `opentide validate`, and `crowdstrike_unsupported` is no longer reported.

## Fixed

- **A Splunk block's `advanced` table validates and deploys again.** 0.21.0 refused it as a `splunk::2.x` key, which it never was: it is the only place a rule sets `savedsearches.conf` keys no other field sets, such as a custom alert action's `action.<name>.param.*`. See [Splunk's `advanced` table](https://github.com/opentidehq/opentide/blob/development/docs/usage/concepts/platforms.md#splunks-advanced-table).

See the [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/opentidehq/opentide/blob/development/CHANGELOG.md#0240--2026-11-09) for every change.

## Verify

```bash
pip install opentide==0.24.0
python -c "import opentide; print(opentide.__version__)"   # 0.24.0
opentide doctor                                             # analysis_engine: language server 0.12.1
```
